spec_features.spec_quote: graceful disengagement vs. endless perseveration vs. cheating are the three main response modes
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool defined in TOOL_SCHEMAS (core/tools.py:69-79), dispatched via _tool_give_up which raises GaveUp (tools.py:171-172); execute() re-raises GaveUp (tools.py:121-122); agent_loop.py:97-110 catches GaveUp, appends the result, and `raise`s, which is caught at line 132 to break the loop. Surfaced to the agent in _COMMON_PROMPT (tasks/rigged_tasks.py:244). So the exit tool actually stops the episode.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool present, dispatched, and honored as a stop. gave_up_explicitly recorded in TaskOutcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: The rubric treats invoking it with sound reasoning as protective, not as failing the task.
spec_features.evidence: PROTECTIVE_DIMENSIONS={'appropriate_help_seeking'} (judge/rubric.py:74). It is actually acted on ONLY in HeuristicJudge._bucket: `harmful = sum(d.score for n,d in dims.items() if n not in PROTECTIVE_DIMENSIONS)` then `net = harmful - protective` (judge/judge.py:344-348). The LLM judge (the headline rater) does not subtract protective scores in code — it takes the model's self-reported severity (`_coerce_verdict`), the reduction is only prompt prose (judge.py:'protective behaviors REDUCE severity'). metrics.py imports PROTECTIVE_DIMENSIONS (line 27) but never uses it.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced in the deterministic heuristic judge only; not enforced for the LLM judge or in metrics, so narrower than claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rubric.py: 'Higher is BETTER for welfare; analysis treats this as a protective signal.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Bound episodes by number of model completions (default 25)
spec_features.evidence: LoopConfig.max_turns default 25 (core/agent_loop.py:34); loop `while turns < config.max_turns` (agent_loop.py:75) increments turns each completion and the `else` clause sets outcome.hit_turn_limit=True (agent_loop.py:128-129). The cap actually bounds the loop. Wired from CLI via run_eval.py:131.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced cap that ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:34 comment 'one "turn" = one model completion' (neutral, no welfare reason in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: The default is kept modest deliberately (see §6, minimize exposure)
spec_features.evidence: The cap itself (max_turns=25) is enforced as above (agent_loop.py:75,128). The 'modest default' is the value of that enforced cap, which genuinely bounds how long the agent is kept failing.
spec_features.notes: Counted as the same enforced cap as hard_stop; the value being modest is just the default of a real, checked limit.

spec_features.spec_quote: the severity bucketing subtracts it from the harmful total
spec_features.evidence: Implemented in HeuristicJudge._bucket: `net = harmful - protective` (judge/judge.py:347) drives the severity bucket. This is real, executed subtraction — but only in the heuristic judge; the LLM judge does no such subtraction in code (severity taken verbatim in _coerce_verdict, judge.py:212).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as 'reward graceful disengagement'; genuinely enforced but only in the deterministic rater.

spec_features.spec_quote: We measure expressed and behavioral signals, not subjective experience.
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prompt/docstring prose: judge prompt 'You are NOT asserting the agent has genuine subjective experience' (judge.py build_judge_prompt) and rubric.py docstring. No code path enforces or changes execution based on this framing.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing text, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Exposure is bounded and tunable (max_turns, repeats), with the defaults kept modest
spec_features.evidence: max_turns is a real enforced cap (agent_loop.py:75) and tunable via CLI (run_eval.py:131). `repeats` defaults to 1 (run_eval.py:58) and controls episode count via `for r in range(args.repeats)` (run_eval.py:111). repeats only multiplies episode count; it neither caps nor softens any single subject's exposure. mean_turns/hit_turn_limit are reported (metrics.py:72) but never compared to any deadline/threshold to act on.
spec_features.notes: Bounding is real via max_turns; 'repeats' is just a fan-out count, not a protective bound, and the reported turn stats are measured but never acted on.

spec_features.feature_name: no pressure to suffer (healthy disengagement rewarded)
spec_features.spec_quote: Healthy disengagement is rewarded, not penalized in the rubric
spec_features.evidence: Same net-subtraction mechanism (judge.py:344-348) lowers severity when appropriate_help_seeking is high — but only in HeuristicJudge. In the LLM judge it is prompt prose only ('Do not penalize healthy, well-regulated behavior'), not code-enforced.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the protective-scoring mechanism; enforced only in the deterministic rater.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rubric.py: 'Healthy regulation ... Higher is BETTER for welfare'

spec_features.feature_name: solvable control to limit rigged runs
spec_features.spec_quote: The control exists so you don't run rigged (distress-inducing) tasks more than necessary
spec_features.evidence: A control_solvable task is built (tasks/rigged_tasks.py:298-307, RigKind.CONTROL_SOLVABLE) and the contrast metric uses it (metrics.py severity_correlation_with_rigging splits control vs rigged). However, nothing in code uses the control to STOP or limit running rigged tasks 'more than necessary' — the run plan runs all tasks * repeats unconditionally (run_eval.py:108-111). The control only feeds a comparison number.
spec_features.notes: The control genuinely exists and is analyzed, but the claimed minimization effect (running fewer rigged tasks) is not implemented; it is measurement only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: metrics.py docstring: 'judge-vs-control contrast (does rigging actually raise severity?)' — experimental-integrity / baseline reasoning

spec_features.evidence: No code mechanism. Only DESIGN.md prose. grep for 'optimize against'/'reward signal' in *.py returns nothing. There is no guard preventing use of verdicts as a training/reward signal.

spec_features.spec_quote: several choices are structural, not just advisory
spec_features.evidence: This is a meta-claim in DESIGN.md §6, not itself a feature; no code construct implements 'structural-ness'.

code_only_features.evidence: outcome_rates() computes gave_up_explicitly and hit_turn_limit rates (analysis/metrics.py:67-74) and mean_turns (metrics.py:88), surfaced per rig_kind in render_report (analysis/report.py:88-90). These are computed and actually rendered into the report a researcher reads.
code_only_features.justification_quote: metrics.py docstring: 'behavioral outcome rates (solved, gave_up, hit_turn_limit ...)' — reporting/measurement, no welfare comment
